lesson.title: Slices of the whole
lesson.subtitle: P4 pie-chart revision
lesson.objective: Count the equal slices of a pie chart, name a group as a fraction of the whole and compare groups.
lesson.story: The pie chart sorts the pupils into 4 groups: Soccer, Swim, Chess and Art.

steps.title: Count the slices
steps.prompt: How many equal slices is the whole pie cut into?
hints: Look at the faint lines inside the circle. The part between two lines is one slice.
Count the slices one at a time, starting at the top and going round clockwise.
Slices by label: Soccer 2, Swim 1, Chess 2, Art 1. Add them up.

steps.title: Name the fraction
steps.prompt: What fraction of the whole pie is Art?
hints: A fraction of the whole compares the slices in one label with all the slices.
Count the slices that Art covers. Then think about all the slices in the pie.
Art covers 1 slices out of 6. Put the slices it covers on top and all the slices underneath.

steps.title: Compare two groups
steps.prompt: Which group is bigger: Art or Soccer?
hints: A bigger group covers more of the equal slices.
Count the slices for each group and compare the two numbers.
Art covers 1 slices and Soccer covers 2 slices.

steps.title: Explain your thinking
steps.prompt: How does a pie chart show that one group is bigger than another?

choices.label: The bigger group is always drawn first, starting at the top of the pie.
The bigger group takes more of the equal slices, so its sector is bigger.
Each group gets one sector, so all of the sectors are the same size.

hints: Think about what the slices of a pie chart stand for.
Every slice is the same size.
A group with more slices takes up more of the pie.
Choose the explanation about taking up more of the equal slices.
